fields.description:
Standardize the CLI write-command argument parsing: retire the hand-rolled loop for Python's stdlib argparse, WITHOUT changing observable behavior. Behavior-preserving MECHANICAL adapter refactor.

## Context / Problem
The CLI parses write-command args with a hand-rolled loop (claim.py `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee`, transition.py `_parse_flags`) carrying bespoke semantics no schema reflects: `--assignee` ABSENT is a None sentinel (=> `ticket.default_assignee` fallback) while explicit `--assignee ""` CLEARS the assignee. Flags and `--help` can silently drift from behavior.

## Dependency / sequencing
Depends on blusterous-earthly-kitten, which normalized the force surface (removed `force_close`; made transition's `--force[=<reason>]` a reason-carrying param matching claim; dropped `--reason`-as-force-note). This refactor must preserve the POST-blusterous surface, so it runs AFTER that change to avoid re-encoding a soon-to-change flag and a conflicting edit on the same files.

## Approach
Refactor onto stdlib argparse (zero new runtime dep, portable, generates accurate `--help`); NOT Click/Typer. Respect the module-size (<=800 LOC) and per-function complexity ratchets by extracting along existing call-graph seams.

### Behavioral fidelity (argparse defaults that MUST be overridden)
The hand loops have load-bearing behaviors argparse does not reproduce by default; preserve each:
- **Unknown/extra tokens are silently skipped** — use `ArgumentParser(add_help=False)` + `parse_known_args()` (not `parse_args()`, which exits 2 on unrecognized args), discarding extras.
- **`--help`/`-h` reconciled with `add_help=False`** — the command detects `-h`/`--help` in argv and prints `parser.format_help()` (exit 0). `--help` is thus GENERATED from the argparse flag definitions (satisfies AC1) while the auto-help action stays off; no contradiction.
- **Prefix-abbreviation disabled** — set `allow_abbrev=False` so `--for`/`--reas` do not match `--force`/`--reason` (the hand loops match exact spellings only).
- **`--force` semantics DIFFER by command — preserve each exactly, do NOT unify:**
  - claim `_parse_force`: `--force=<x>` -> x (empty -> "(no reason given)"); bare `--force` consumes the FOLLOWING token as the reason iff it does NOT start with `--`, else "(no reason given)". argparse's default handling differs on a following option-like token, so enforce the following-token/`--`-guard explicitly.
  - transition `_parse_flags`: `--force=<x>` -> x (incl. empty -> ""); bare `--force` -> "" and MUST NOT consume the following token (a direct-caller test, test_force_does_not_swallow_a_following_token, pins this). Reason on transition is supplied only via `--force=<reason>`.
- **`--assignee` accepts `--assignee=<val>` AND space-separated `--assignee <val>` (next token consumed unconditionally); value-less at end exits 1** ("Error: --assignee requires a value"). Preserve None-vs-"" sentinel: ABSENT -> None; present (incl. "") -> that value.
- **Retired `--force-close` keeps its exit-1 rejection** — transition rejects `--force-close`/`--force-close=<x>` with a bespoke message (test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py); argparse would silently skip it, so re-add an explicit pre/post-parse `CommandError(returncode=1)` with the existing message + rename guidance.
- **Value-less/invalid-flag errors exit 1 with the current messages**, not argparse's default exit-2 + usage — use `exit_on_error=False` and/or catch `SystemExit`/`argparse.ArgumentError` and re-raise `CommandError(returncode=1)`.

## Preserving direct callers of the private parse helpers
`transition._parse_flags` is imported and called directly (unpacking its exact 5-tuple `(reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref)`, pinning None-vs-'' and the retired-flag rejection) by three tests OUTSIDE src/rebar/_commands/: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_ref_target_80af.py, tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py, tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py. To keep them passing UNCHANGED, `_parse_flags` is RETAINED as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple/semantics. claim's `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee` have no external direct callers (grep-verified) and may be replaced freely provided CLI-observable behavior is preserved.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/claim.py — replace `_parse_force`/`_parse_assignee` with an argparse-backed parser, preserving the `--assignee` None-vs-"" sentinel.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition.py — replace `_parse_flags`' hand loop with an argparse-backed parser, RETAINING `_parse_flags` as a shim returning the same 5-tuple.
- Lib and MCP surfaces are OUT OF SCOPE (adapter-local change).

## Testing
- Existing CLI interface tests pass unchanged (tests/interfaces), incl. test_close_ref_target_80af.py's direct `_parse_flags` call (preserved via the shim).
- Direct-caller unit/script tests pass unchanged: test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py (None-vs-'' + retired `--force-close` rejection), test_dependency_audit.py.
- `--force[=<reason>]` inline + space-separated forms; bare -> "(no reason given)"; `--reason` only close_reason, never the force note.
- `--assignee` absent => default_assignee fallback; "" => cleared; value-less => exit 1.
- Unknown tokens silently skipped; retired `--force-close` exits 1; abbreviations do not match; ConcurrencyError exits 10.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLI write-command parsing goes through argparse and `--help` is GENERATED from the flag definitions: with `add_help=False`, the command detects `-h`/`--help` and prints `parser.format_help()` (verified functionally by running --help and confirming it lists the flags; no byte-exact help golden is asserted).
- [ ] The `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying form is preserved (bare -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason); `--reason` is not repurposed as the force note (test).
- [ ] The `--assignee` None-vs-empty-string distinction is preserved: absent => default_assignee fallback, "" => cleared (test asserts both).
- [ ] `transition._parse_flags` is retained as an argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple, so its three external direct callers pass unchanged.
- [ ] `--force` command-specific semantics preserved: claim bare `--force` -> next non-`--` token else "(no reason given)"; transition bare `--force` -> "" and does NOT swallow a following token (reason only via `--force=<x>`). `--assignee` accepts inline `=value` AND a space-separated next token (consumed unconditionally), value-less => exit 1. `allow_abbrev=False` so partial spellings do not match (tests).
- [ ] argparse behavioral fidelity: unknown/extra tokens silently skipped (parse_known_args), retired `--force-close` keeps its exit-1 rejection, and value-less/invalid-flag errors exit 1 with existing messages (not argparse's exit-2 + usage).
- [ ] Exit code 10 on ConcurrencyError is preserved (existing CLI interface tests pass).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green; module-size and complexity ratchets respected.
